extracted.intended_audience: politically-engaged English readers (18th century); subscribers/readers of the Public Advertiser; citizens concerned with constitutional liberties
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical political pamphlet/letter assessing the conduct of ministers, judges, and the sovereign with respect to constitutional principles, jury rights, press freedom, and public virtue. The text argues standards by which public officers and institutions should be judged and condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers as public servants, not private domestics
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers are no longer the public servants of the state, but the private domestics of the sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ministers by whether they serve the public interest and constitution or act as personal agents/favourites of the sovereign; criticism and examples of favouritism (a class of men permitted to call themselves the king's friends) are offered as anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of election as fundamental right
rubrics_metrics.description: The free election of our representatives in parliament comprehends, because it is, the source and security of every right and privilege of the English nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any measure violating the freedom of election should be treated as striking at all liberties (example: Middlesex election); assess governmental acts by their effect on electoral freedom and representative rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abuse/prostitution of the prerogative and unconstitutional military employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The odious abuse and prostitution of the prerogative at home; the unconstitutional employment of the military; the arbitrary fines and commitments by the house of lords and court of king's bench.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge government harshly when prerogative is prostituted, military is used unconstitutionally, or when arbitrary fines/commitments occur; these are presented as signs of serious constitutional decay and should provoke public indignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and conduct expected of a sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The morality of a king is not to be measured by vulgar rules. His situation is singular: there are faults which do him honour, and virtues that disgrace him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a monarch by whether seclusion, narrow attachments, or ignorance produce bigotry and misgovernment; a sovereign should be open to better information and new connections rather than being secluded with favourites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial fidelity to common law and constitutional documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In contempt or ignorance of the common law of England, you have made it your study to introduce into the court where you preside, maxims of jurisprudence unknown to Englishmen ... who ever heard you mention Magna Charta, or the Bill of Rights, with approbation or respect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges should be evaluated on fidelity to Magna Carta, Bill of Rights, and common-law traditions rather than importing foreign codes (Roman law) or civilian opinions; divergence from these is criticized as corrupting English liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges must not contract or usurp jury power
rubrics_metrics.description: You have made it your study ... to contract the power of the jury, or to mislead their judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper judge respects the province of the jury; attempts to constrict jurors' role or mislead them (especially in libel and criminal cases) are unconstitutional and threaten liberties. Assess charges and instructions that remove facts or malice from juries' consideration as abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court of King's Bench should not become a court of equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The court of king's bench becomes a court of equity; and the judge, instead of consulting strictly the law of the land, refers only to the wisdom of the court, and to the purity of his own conscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial decisions should follow settled legal rules rather than amorphous equity or a judge's private conscience; evaluate judgments that substitute subjective notions of equity for law as dangerous precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury competence in libel cases — right to consider malice/intent
rubrics_metrics.description: When you invade the province of the jury, in matter of libel, you, in effect, attack the liberty of the press ... In other criminal prosecutions, the malice of the design is confessedly as much the subject of consideration to a jury as the certainty of the fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In libel trials, juries should consider both fact and malice/intent; removing the jury's authority on malice is tantamount to destroying press liberty. Evaluate libel charges by whether juries retain this competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on packing juries / peremptory challenges by judge
rubrics_metrics.description: Without offering any legal objection, you ordered a special juryman to be set aside, in a cause where the king was prosecutor. Will you condescend to tell the world by what law or custom you were authorized to make a peremptory challenge of a juryman?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is improper for a judge or party to peremptorily challenge or pack juries in favor of the crown; such acts should be recorded and condemned as attempts to corrupt justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial consistency and adherence to legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Your charge to the jury ... contradicts the highest legal authorities, as well as the plainest dictates of reason. In Miller's case, and still more expressly in that of Baldwin, you have proceeded a step farther, and grossly contradicted yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess judicial instructions for consistency with precedent and legal authorities; contradictory or self-serving charges that depart from established doctrine indicate abuse of judicial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to prosecutorial use to silence the press
rubrics_metrics.description: The distress and danger with which the press is threatened, when your lordship is party, and the party is to be judge ... the liberty of the press ... is wounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prosecutions of printers/press by whether they are used to stifle criticism; prosecution of the press by interested parties or judges acting as parties is illegitimate and a threat to public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of peers/ministers to defend constitution regardless of party neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws and constitution are the general property of the subject — not to defend, is to relinquish: and who is there so senseless as to renounce his share in a common benefit, unless he hopes to profit by a new division of the spoil?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peers and ministers cannot hide behind neutrality; they have a duty to act to defend constitutional rights. Evaluate public officers by whether they actively protect constitutional safeguards rather than skulk into private influence.
